Let $1 \le k < q$ with $s_k \ge 2$ and $s_j = 0$ for all $k < j \le q$. Then the number of partitions of $n(q, s)$ with diagonal…
nodes.title: Truncating the staircase of a diagonal sequence

Put $L = q + s_1 + \dots + s_q$. If $s_i \ge 2$ for all $1 \le i < q$, then exactly one partition of $n$ with…
nodes.title: Diagonal classes whose multiplicities are at least two

nodes.summary: Let $q \ge 0$ and let $s_1, \dots, s_q$ be natural numbers. The conjugate of the partition $\bar\alpha$ with parts $\bar\alpha_i = q - i + 1 + \sum_{k=i}^{q} s_k$ for $1 \le i \le q$ is the partition $\underline{\alpha} = (q^{(s_q + 1)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1} + 1)}, \dots, 1^{(s_1 + 1)})$, where $v^{(r)}$ means $r$ copies of $v$; the parts are compared as multisets.
nodes.title: Conjugate of a partition with prescribed gaps between its parts

nodes.summary: The conjugate of the partition with parts $\{3, 1\}$ is the partition with parts $\{2, 1, 1\}$.
nodes.title: The conjugate of $(3, 1)$ is $(2, 1, 1)$

nodes.summary: For a finite multiset $\alpha$ of natural numbers with largest element $m$ (and $m = 0$ if $\alpha$ is empty), the conjugate $\alpha^*$ is the multiset of the $m$ numbers $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{m-1}$, where $c_j$ is the number of elements of $\alpha$ greater than $j$, counted with multiplicity. When $\alpha$ is the multiset of parts of a partition, these are the parts of the conjugate partition.
nodes.title: Conjugate of a multiset of parts

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partition of $n \ge 1$, let $d = \delta(\alpha)$ be its diagonal sequence, written without its trailing zeros, and let $[\alpha]$ be the set of partitions of $n$ with diagonal sequence $d$, each written by its parts in decreasing order. Here $v^{(r)}$ means $r$ copies of $v$, and a run $a, a - 1, \dots, b$ with $a < b$ is empty. (1) If $|[\alpha]| = 1$, then there is $q \ge 1$ with…
nodes.title: Diagonal classes of size at most three

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a sequence $d = (d_k)_{k \ge 0}$ of natural numbers, $[d]$ is the finite set of partitions $\beta$ of $n$ whose diagonal sequence $\delta(\beta)$ equals $d$.
nodes.title: Partitions with a prescribed diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: For a partition $p$ of $n$, its diagonal class $\delta^{-1}(\delta(p))$ is the finite set of all partitions $\beta$ of $n$ whose diagonal sequence $\delta(\beta)$ equals the diagonal sequence $\delta(p)$ of $p$.
nodes.title: Diagonal class of a partition

nodes.summary: For $q = 4$ and $s_1 = 1$, $s_2 = 1$, $s_3 = 0$, $s_4 = 2$, the maximal partition $\bar\alpha$, with parts $\bar\alpha_i = q - i + 1 + \sum_{k=i}^{q} s_k$ for $1 \le i \le q$, is $(8, 6, 4, 3)$.
nodes.title: Maximal partition for $q = 4$ and $s = (1, 1, 0, 2)$

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a partition of $n$, let $q$ be a natural number and $s = (s_k)$ a sequence of natural numbers, and suppose that the diagonal sequence of $p$ is $(1, 2, \dots, q, q^{(s_q)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1})}, \dots, 1^{(s_1)})$ followed by zeros, where $v^{(m)}$ denotes $m$ copies of $v$. Let $\alpha$ be the parts of $p$ in decreasing order, let $\bar\alpha = (\bar\alpha_1, \dots, \bar\alpha_q)$ with…
nodes.title: The diagonal class lies between the maximal and minimal partitions in majorization

nodes.summary: Let $q > 0$ and let $s_1, \dots, s_q$ be natural numbers with $q(q+1)/2 + \sum_{k=1}^{q} k s_k = n$, and let $\bar\alpha = (\bar\alpha_1, \dots, \bar\alpha_q)$ with $\bar\alpha_i = q - i + 1 + \sum_{k=i}^{q} s_k$. Then the entries of $\bar\alpha$ are positive, sum to $n$ and are strictly decreasing; the diagonal sequence of $\bar\alpha$ is $(1, 2, \dots, q, q^{(s_q)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1})}, \dots, 1^{(s_1)})$ followed…
nodes.title: The maximal partition has the prescribed diagonal normal form

nodes.summary: For a natural number $q$ and a sequence $s = (s_k)$ of natural numbers, $\bar\alpha = (\bar\alpha_1, \dots, \bar\alpha_q)$ is the list of the $q$ numbers $\bar\alpha_i = q - i + 1 + \sum_{k=i}^{q} s_k$, $1 \le i \le q$, in this order.
nodes.title: Maximal partition of a diagonal normal form
Minimal partition for $q = 4$ and $s = (1, 1, 0, 2)$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $q$ and a sequence $s = (s_k)$ of natural numbers, $\underline\alpha$ is the list $(q^{(s_q + 1)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1} + 1)}, \dots, 1^{(s_1 + 1)})$, where $v^{(m)}$ denotes $m$ copies of $v$: first $s_q + 1$ copies of $q$, then $s_{q-1} + 1$ copies of $q - 1$, and so on down to $s_1 + 1$ copies of $1$.
nodes.title: Minimal partition of a diagonal normal form
Diagonal normal form for $q = 4$ and $s = (1, 1, 0, 2)$

nodes.summary: For a natural number $q$ and a sequence $s = (s_k)$ of natural numbers, the normal form is the list $(1, 2, \dots, q - 1, q, q^{(s_q)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1})}, \dots, 1^{(s_1)})$, where $v^{(m)}$ denotes $m$ copies of $v$: the numbers $1, \dots, q$ followed by $s_v$ copies of $v$ for $v = q, q - 1, \dots, 1$.
nodes.title: Normal form of a diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: The sequence given by the list $(1, 2, 1)$ takes the values $0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 0$ at the indices $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$.
nodes.title: The list sequence of $(1, 2, 1)$

nodes.summary: A finite list $(d_1, \dots, d_\ell)$ of natural numbers determines the sequence of natural numbers whose value at index $k$ is $d_k$ for $1 \le k \le \ell$, and $0$ for $k = 0$ and for $k > \ell$. This is the indexing of diagonal sequences, which take the value $0$ at index $0$.
nodes.title: Sequence of a finite list

nodes.summary: Let $q \ge 0$ and $s_1, \dots, s_q \ge 0$ be natural numbers, write $v^{(m)}$ for $m$ copies of $v$, and let $\bar\alpha$ and $\underline\alpha$ be the partitions with parts $\bar\alpha_i = q - i + 1 + s_i + s_{i+1} + \dots + s_q$ for $1 \le i \le q$ and $\underline\alpha = (q^{(s_q + 1)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1} + 1)}, \dots, 1^{(s_1 + 1)})$. Then $\bar\alpha$ and $\underline\alpha$ have the same diagonal sequence; this…
nodes.title: Equal diagonal sequences of the maximal and minimal partitions

nodes.summary: The diagonal sequence of the partition $(7, 7, 4, 1, 1, 1)$ takes the values $0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 4, 2, 1, 0$ at the indices $0, 1, \dots, 9$. This is the paper's running example.
nodes.title: Diagonal sequence of $(7, 7, 4, 1, 1, 1)$

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partition of $n$ with diagonal sequence $(d_k)_{k \ge 0}$, where $d_0 = 0$, and let $k \ge 0$. Then $d_{k+1} \le d_k + 1$, with equality if and only if $d_j = j$ for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le k + 1$. Moreover, if $d_{k+1} \le d_k$, then $d_{k+2} \le d_{k+1}$.
nodes.title: Increments of the diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partition with parts $\alpha_1 \ge \alpha_2 \ge \dots \ge \alpha_t$, and set $\alpha_i = 0$ for $i > t$. Its diagonal sequence $\delta(\alpha) = (d_k)_{k \ge 0}$ has $d_0 = 0$ and, for $k \ge 1$, $d_k$ equal to the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i \le k$ and $\alpha_i + i - 1 \ge k$, that is, the number of cells of the Young diagram on its $k$-th diagonal from upper right to lower left.…
nodes.title: Diagonal sequence of a partition

nodes.summary: For every positive integer $m$ there are a natural number $n$ and a partition $\alpha$ of $n$ whose class, the set of partitions of $n$ with the same diagonal sequence as $\alpha$, has exactly $m$ elements.
nodes.title: Every positive integer is the size of a diagonal class

Let $\alpha$ be a partition of $n$ with parts $\alpha_1 \ge \dots \ge \alpha_t$,…
nodes.title: Repeated parts and large gaps in a diagonal class

nodes.summary: Write $v^{(m)}$ for $m$ copies of $v$. For every partition $\alpha$ of $n \ge 1$ there are an integer $q > 0$ and natural numbers $s_1, \dots, s_q$ such that the diagonal sequence of $\alpha$, indexed from $0$, is $(0, 1, 2, \dots, q, q^{(s_q)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1})}, \dots, 1^{(s_1)}, 0, 0, \dots)$ and $q(q+1)/2 + \sum_{k=1}^{q} k s_k = n$. Moreover $q$ and $s_1, \dots, s_q$ are unique: if $q' > 0$ and…
nodes.title: Existence and uniqueness of the diagonal normal form

nodes.summary: Every partition $\beta$ of $n$ belongs to the set of partitions of $n$ whose diagonal sequence equals that of $\beta$.
nodes.title: A partition lies in the class of its diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: For every partition $p$ of $n$, $p$ belongs to the diagonal class of $p$, the set of partitions of $n$ whose diagonal sequence equals that of $p$.
nodes.title: Every partition lies in its diagonal class

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, including $n = 0$, the number of distinct diagonal sequences of partitions of $n$ equals the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts, and the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts equals the number of partitions of $n$ into odd parts.
nodes.title: Counting diagonal sequences

nodes.summary: For partitions $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $n$, with parts listed in decreasing order, $\alpha$ majorizes $\beta$ if and only if the conjugate partition $\beta^*$ majorizes the conjugate partition $\alpha^*$, again with parts listed in decreasing order.
nodes.title: Conjugation reverses majorization

nodes.summary: The partition $(3, 1)$ majorizes the partition $(2, 2)$: $3 \ge 2$ and $3 + 1 \ge 2 + 2$.
nodes.title: Majorization of $(2, 2)$ by $(3, 1)$

nodes.summary: For finite lists $a = (a_1, \dots, a_s)$ and $b = (b_1, \dots, b_t)$ of natural numbers, $a$ majorizes $b$, written $a \succ b$, when $b_1 + \dots + b_k \le a_1 + \dots + a_k$ for every natural number $k \le \min\{s, t\}$.
nodes.title: Majorization of part lists

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partition of $n$ with diagonal sequence $(d_k)_{k \ge 1}$ and conjugate partition $\alpha^*$, and write $s(\gamma)$ for the sum of the squares of the parts of a partition $\gamma$. Then $s(\alpha) + s(\alpha^*) = 2 \sum_{k=1}^{2n} k \, d_k$. Consequently every partition $\beta$ of $n$ with the same diagonal sequence as $\alpha$ satisfies $s(\beta) + s(\beta^*) = s(\alpha) + s(\alpha^*)$.
nodes.title: Sums of squared parts and the diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a partition of $n$, let $q$ and $s_1, s_2, \dots$ be natural numbers, and suppose the diagonal sequence of $\alpha$ is $(1, 2, \dots, q, q^{(s_q)}, (q-1)^{(s_{q-1})}, \dots, 1^{(s_1)})$ followed by zeros, where $v^{(m)}$ denotes $m$ copies of $v$. Then the largest part of $\alpha$ (taken to be $0$ if $\alpha$ has no parts) lies in the set $A_1 = \{q + \sum_{i=j}^{q} s_i : 1 \le j \le q + 1\}$, that…
nodes.title: The largest part of a partition with given diagonal sequence

nodes.summary: For every integer $a$ and every natural number $t \ge 1$, the set $\{a, a + 1, \dots, a + t - 1\}$ of $t$ consecutive integers has exactly $2^{t-1}$ vn-arrangements, that is, orderings $(v_1, \dots, v_t)$ of its elements with $v_{i+1} - v_i \le 1$ for all $i$.
nodes.title: Vn-arrangements of consecutive integers

nodes.summary: Let $k \le t$ be natural numbers, let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be natural numbers, and let $M$ be the multiset of integers containing $b_i$ copies of $i$ for each $0 \le i \le t$, so that $M$ has $m = b_0 + \dots + b_t$ elements. Then the number of $k$-vn-arrangements of $M$, that is, orderings $(v_1, \dots, v_m)$ of $M$ with $v_{j+1} - v_j \le k$ for all $j$, is
nodes.title: Counting $k$-vn-arrangements of a multiset

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a natural number, let $b_0, b_1, \dots$ be natural numbers, and let $M$ be the multiset of integers containing $b_i$ copies of $i$ for each $0 \le i \le t$, so that $M$ has $m = b_0 + \dots + b_t$ elements. Then the number of vn-arrangements of $M$, that is, orderings $(v_1, \dots, v_m)$ of $M$ with $v_{j+1} - v_j \le 1$ for all $j$, is $\prod_{i=0}^{t-1} \binom{b_i + b_{i+1}}{b_i}$.
nodes.title: Counting vn-arrangements of a multiset

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$ and every integer $a$, the one-element multiset $\{a\}$ has exactly one $k$-vn-arrangement.
nodes.title: A singleton multiset has one $k$-vn-arrangement

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and $M$ a finite multiset of integers. A $k$-vn-arrangement of $M$ is a finite sequence $(v_1, \dots, v_b)$ of integers whose multiset of entries is $M$ and with $v_{i+1} - v_i \le k$ for all $1 \le i < b$. This is the number of distinct such sequences; sequences are compared entry by entry, so exchanging two equal entries gives the same arrangement. For $k = 1$ these are the…
nodes.title: Number of $k$-vn-arrangements

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
